name: Memory Management
summary: What the assistant remembers about you, where you see it, and how you correct or remove it.
overview: Memory is the set of health details the assistant has been told, kept between conversations so a user does not have to re-explain their situation every time.

It is four screens. The list groups everything it holds and opens a summary of what it knows; a memory opens as its own page; a field opens as a sheet over that page; and deleting is a dialog that says what deleting does and does not take with it.
Viewing moved from a bottom sheet to a pushed page in this round, which changes how getting back works and is the main thing to confirm against the build.

states.name: Memory
states.description: The whole set, grouped: seven groups and thirty-two memories under a summary of what the assistant has been told.

states.name: Selecting
states.description: Select turns every row into a choice: a checkbox at the left, Select all and Cancel in the bar, and a Delete that counts what is ticked.

states.name: Viewing a memory
states.description: One memory as a pushed page — its category, the memory, when it changed, where it came from, and the fields it is made of.

states.name: Editing a memory
states.description: One field at a time, in a sheet over the page, with the keyboard up and the required caption under the input.

states.name: Deleting a memory
states.description: The confirmation, naming the consequence: the detail can be saved again, and chat history is untouched.

states.name: After deletion
states.description: The list afterwards, with a toast naming what happened. A memory drawn in two groups leaves both.

behaviour.detail: A single statement in the user's own framing — “You’re 8 weeks pregnant”, “You have a peanut allergy” — carrying a category, a last-updated date, and a link to the conversation or file it came from.
A written summary paragraph set, and the individual memories as list rows. The summary carries its own “Last updated today”; whether it regenerates when a memory is edited is not stated.
Memories sit under titled groups — Top of mind, Your current health, Your vaccines — separated by 1px #DDDFEB rules. The same memory appears under more than one group.
Every memory states where it came from and offers the originating chat as a tappable citation. File-derived memories say “from a file upload”; chat-derived ones say “from a chat”.
Delete asks for confirmation and offers to also delete the chat the memory started in, defaulted off. The chat is kept unless that box is checked.
An “Edit memory” action exists on the detail sheet. What it opens is not drawn.
When new information contradicts a held memory the assistant raises an inline card naming the category, not the values. Reviewing opens a sheet with the existing memory above the suggested one.
The card offers “Not now”; the sheet offers “Don’t update”. The declined branch leaves no trace in the transcript, and the assistant keeps the old memory.
Uploading a document asks permission before details are retained, at three levels — always, this time, never. Two competing treatments are drawn: a modal dialog and an in-chat choice list.
“Always remember” sets a standing preference. No surface is drawn where it can be reviewed or turned off.
Every frame shows a populated account. Nothing is drawn for a user who has no memories yet.
Search sits in the nav beside Select, where it used to be a pill pinned over the foot of the list. The surface it opens is not drawn.

The V1 handoff file carries an Incognito Mode block stating that activity is not saved and conversations will not appear in history. It is hidden at opacity 0 on both Conversation History frames and has no counterpart in the September Launch Memory designs.
